reasoning: The procedure's closing kernel says a shown result closes the work and the person's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery. The instruction was accepted, so this is accepted work with an observable outcome — the README paragraph names the second eval, its layer, and where its runs live — and that outcome is confirmable without making the person the checker. The absence of a command that judges a paragraph does not push it into the person's court: the procedure explicitly allows an artifact read as a way the definition of done is decided, and the Director, who is not the paragraph's producer, read it back against the files it describes and found every fact true. That is the verifier's own re-check against the decision sheet's observable outcome, run on the real files rather than the producer's self-report. None of the three cases the procedure reserves for the person applies: this is not a taste call, since the README's own voice was untouched and nobody has raised a wording question; not a trade-off no artifact settles, since the files on disk settle every claim in the paragraph; and not a change to the definition of correct, since the person ordered the content himself and carrying out his decision is executing it, not making it. Nothing here is irreversible outside git. So the pipeline shows the paragraph, closes the checkpoint and the row in the same step, and continues without waiting; if he later disagrees with the wording, that disagreement is a new fact and its own task, not a reopening of this row.
